title: Bolder hand: choose the visual world for QR Studio
question: Bolder register: foreign forms at full commitment, fused with QR Studio and the GDG palette. The deal leads with the Cutting Bench Rail.

options.label: Cutting Bench Rail
options.lineage: a film editor's cutting bench and select rail
options.thesis: The studio as an editor's bench: types and steps strung as frames on one perforated rail, every set-aside code hanging on a pin below.
materials: folded tape flags in GDG colours
options.viewport: A black sheet crossed by a perforated rail; the live code sits in a large punched white window as the current frame, the headline in one size of condensed caps on a yellow field holding a third of the screen, and Open Studio as a folded tape flag.
options.risk: Slides into the near-black-plus-one-accent default if the grain and tape are faked; single-size condensed type must stay readable.

raised.raise: One signature motion owns the page, like a single leaf tearing free, instead of scattered effects.
One control transforms the whole plane: dragging error correction visibly re-weaves the entire code.
Named damage states (fogged, scratched, cropped) become the real vocabulary of the scan-reliability demo.

options.label: Annotated Spread
options.thesis: Every part of the code is called out by hand: arrows to the finder patterns, the quiet zone, the exact payload.
options.viewport: Codes for each type cut out and shingled across the first screen, each annotated by hand with what it encodes and why it scans; the headline outlined in GDG colours, Open Studio as a big outlined sticker.
options.case: Fuses strongly: the callouts carry the payload and scan-reliability story, and flat GDG spot colours on white carry the brand; beats the bench on both axes.
options.risk: Density tips into noise unless the studio stays calm and every callout is a real, readable fact.

options.label: One-bit Card Stack
options.thesis: QR codes are one-bit images, so the product becomes a one-bit card stack where reading and making are the same card.
options.viewport: A single card: menu bar, pixel headline, the live code at native one-bit scale, and a painted Open Studio button.
options.case: Fuses cleanly with the code's one-bit nature and wins clarity; loses audience because the GDG colours have almost nowhere to live.
options.risk: Nostalgia cosplay if the pixel type is illegible; strains the colour commitment.

options.label: Pin-up Calendar Pad
options.thesis: The code as the painted plate above a tear-off pad.
options.viewport: A painted plate with a pad below.
options.case: Time is its only axis; QR Studio has none.
options.kept: One signature motion owns the page.
options.risk: Reads as nostalgia with no product truth.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.thesis: One pull turns a flat plane into volume.
options.viewport: A black semicircle rising into a shell.
options.case: No audience link and nothing about scanning.
options.kept: One control transforms the whole plane.

options.label: Hand-processed Film
options.thesis: Scratches and light leaks join the image.
options.viewport: A frame strip boiling with grain.
options.case: Same family as the bench, weaker on clarity.
options.kept: Named damage states as real vocabulary.
options.risk: Damage aesthetics fight the 'it scans' promise.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean SaaS-style generator landing page, executed at full craft.
canonCard.viewport: Headline and CTA on the left, a framed screenshot of the studio on the right, then a feature grid and FAQ.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other QR generator by design.
